subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT generally used in milk adulteration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Saw dust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Saw dust** is a type of fine powder or small particles of wood that are produced during activities like sawing, sanding, or milling.

• Saw dust is **not generally used** in milk adulteration because it does not dissolve in milk and can be easily detected.

• Common adulterants in milk include urea, starch, and detergent, which are used to increase the thickness and shelf life of milk.

• Using non-dissolvable substances like saw dust would make the milk appear visibly contaminated, making it impractical for adulteration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Urea:**

• Urea is a nitrogen-containing compound that is often added to milk to increase its protein content artificially.

• It can be harmful if consumed in large quantities, as it can cause kidney damage and other health issues.

• **Starch:**

• Starch is sometimes added to milk to increase its thickness and viscosity, making it appear richer and creamier.

• Excessive starch can lead to digestive problems and is an indicator of milk adulteration.

• **Detergent:**

• Detergents are added to milk to create froth and give the appearance of high-fat content.

• Consuming milk with detergent can be dangerous and lead to gastrointestinal issues and other health problems.

• **Milk Adulteration:**

• Milk adulteration is the process of adding foreign substances to milk to increase its volume or improve its appearance.

• Common adulterants include water, urea, detergent, starch, and synthetic milk.

• Adulteration is harmful and can pose significant health risks to consumers.

• Regulatory bodies and food safety authorities actively monitor and test milk samples to prevent and detect adulteration.
